newsitem.title: USA: Ford's Hertz sees up to $480 million from offering.
newsitem.headline: Ford's Hertz sees up to $480 million from offering.

text.p: Car rental giant Hertz Corp., a unit of Ford Motor Co., said Thursday it expects to raise about $420 million to $480 million in its long-awaited initial public offering.

In a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission in Washington, Hertz said it expects to sell up to 20.01 million shares, at an estimated offering price of $21 to $24 a share. The offering represents about 18.6 percent of Hertz' total equity.
Hertz will use proceeds of the offering to finance a $460 million dividend it paid to Ford on Feb. 27.
A Ford spokesman said the offering could take place by the end of March. Hertz shares will trade on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol HRZ.

Hertz, based in Park Ridge, N.J., said in the filing that the 20.01-million-share offering includes a 2.6 million-share overallotment option granted to underwriters, which are being led by J.P. Morgan & Co. Other underwriters include Lehman Brothers, Salomon Brothers Inc., Goldman Sachs & Co. and Smith Barney Inc.
Of the 17.4 million shares excluding the overallotment option, about 90 percent will be offered in the United States, and 10 percent will be offered overseas.

Ford, which will retain about 95.3 percent of the voting control over Hertz, currently intends to continue to hold its remaining Hertz shares once the offering is complete, Hertz said in the filing. Following the offering, if overallotment options are exercised, Ford will own 51.9 percent of Hertz' Class A shares and all of its Class B shares.
